rationale: PINS the boundary of the canonical `decorates` edge (RelationshipType.Decorates, landed in src/ast/types.ts df5a03eb2): one row per decorator, source = the decorated declaration, target = the DECORATOR name leaf, line = the decorator's own line — never a row for a name used as the decorator's ARGUMENT. `@inject(make())` emits decorates method -> inject at line 19 and NOTHING for `make` (no decorates row, no calls row: the call/read walks suppress decorator position whole). DISCRIMINATION is built in so a too-broad rule fails instead of passing: `pool = make()` in the field INITIALIZER is a genuine call from the class and must survive, and `return make` in the method body is a genuine read — decorator position is positional, not 'anything near an @'. The parameter-decorator position is NOT covered because ECMAScript decorators (and this grammar) have no parameter decorators: there is no syntax to emit from.
